papers.title: Mathematical Blueprint and 240-Declaration Kernel Index for the Alpöge–Claude Lean 4 Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: On 20 November 2026, Levent Alpöge released a commentless Lean 4 formalization, developed with Claude, proving the Riemann hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for all Dirichlet $L$-functions across $175{,}187$ source modules ($17{,}374{,}215$ lines; $1{,}484{,}733$ compiled kernel declarations). While independent kernel replays confirm formal validity from the three standard Lean axioms, no conventional mathematical paper accompanied the archive. We give a compact, self-contained five-stage mathematical blueprint of the argument from a windowed prime-power inequality to the five root theorems of Main.lean, anchored to an index of $240$ kernel-live declarations ($233$ public declarations across $104$ modules plus $7$ structure fields and Mathlib theorems), each pinned by exact source line, kernel export_id, and five-root reachability bitmask in solution.ndjson. First, a gamma-localized Landau derivative dichotomy excludes zeros in $\operatorname{Re} s > \theta$ from a one-sided bound $G_{\mathcal{F}}(y) \le C y^\theta$ on arbitrarily distant windows $[Z, Z^{3/2}]$ without global sign assumptions. Second, character orthogonality on $G = (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2 \times H$ over CM towers of degree $[E:\mathbb{Q}] = 4n \asymp x^{2+8\varepsilon}$ isolates odd inert prime powers via $\mathrm{ASK} - \mathrm{MAIN} = \mathrm{De}$. Third, along an $m$-step unitary theta ladder ($m \asymp x^{1/2-\varepsilon/16}$, $k \asymp x^{9/2+10\varepsilon}$), supersingular height-$2$ Lubin-Tate formal groups supply net $\ell$-adic jet valuation rate $\gamma_\ell = \frac{1}{\ell - 1} - \frac{1}{\ell^2 - 1} = \frac{\ell}{\ell^2 - 1} = \sum_{e\,\mathrm{odd}} \ell^{-e}$ against rate $0$ at split primes. Fourth, averaging a four-clause Bost-Arakelov slope chain with Chowla-Selberg CM period evaluation cancels intermediate heights, while block-shared divisor budgets replace $O(m^2)$ prefix compounding ($x^{2/3}$ barrier) by $O(m)$; a four-wall linear program over $(a, \kappa)$ at $\nu = 2$ uniquely selects $(a, \kappa) = (1/2, 9/2)$ and $\theta_* = 1/2$. We also record three classical consequences, resolve archive homonym collisions, and verify $27$ companion algebraic, LP, Lubin-Tate, slope-telescope, and carrier-isomorphism theorems in a zero-import Lean 4.33.1 module.

papers.title: Exact, total and filtered small categories
papers.abstract: For a non-empty connected small category we compare four properties: being filtered; exactness of colimits of abelian groups; Grothendieck's total asphericity, which says that colimits of simplicial sets over the category are homotopy colimits; and being quasi-filtered, which means that two arrows with a common source can be completed to a commutative square and that two parallel arrows are equalized by an integral combination of arrows whose coefficients sum to 1. Each implies the next. We give a category of finite ordered hypergraphs that is totally aspherical and whose colimits are exact over no non-zero ring, and we show that the category of finite ordered two-graphs (sets of triples that meet every four-element set in an even number of triples) is quasi-filtered and not totally aspherical. With the example of Isbell and Mitchell, the three implications are strict. A conjecture in Grothendieck's Les Dérivateurs, that totally aspherical categories are filtered, is therefore false; it holds for sifted categories, those over which colimits of sets commute with finite products.

papers.title: The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid is a group, on a question of Lochak and Schneps
papers.abstract: An element of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ of Drinfeld is a pair $(\lambda,f)$, with $\lambda$ a unit of $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f$ in the free profinite group $\widehat F_2$ on $x$ and $y$, that satisfies three relations and for which $x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$ is an automorphism of $\widehat F_2$. Lochak and Schneps asked in 2006 whether this last requirement follows from the others, and whether it holds with no relation at all (Question 1.1 of their list of open problems). We prove that it follows, and from less: if $\lambda\in1+2\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f\in\widehat F_2$ satisfy the two-cycle and three-cycle relations (I) and (II), then $\lambda$ is a unit and the endomorphism is an automorphism. The pentagon relation is not used. Relation (I) alone does not suffice: for $\lambda=1$ and $f=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ the endomorphism is not surjective. It follows that the Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid, in the profinite form of Horel and of Boavida de Brito, Horel and Robertson, is equal to its group of units; that every endomorphism of the profinite operad of parenthesized braids that fixes the objects is an automorphism; and, by their theorems, that every homotopy endomorphism of the profinite completion of the little 2-discs operad, or of the genus zero surface operad, is a homotopy automorphism. The proof counts boundary components of finite covers in homology. An endomorphism of the profinite completion of the fundamental group of a compact surface with boundary that sends every boundary generator to a conjugate of a unit power of a boundary generator, bijectively on boundary components, is an automorphism; on a sphere with at least three holes the exponents of such an endomorphism are equal, and are zero or a unit. The criterion for unit exponents and the case of unit $\lambda$ were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high. Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max checked them again, found the statements for exponents that are not assumed to be units and the example above, and wrote this text. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked these additions independently. No human has checked any of it.

papers.title: A constant gap for the maximal cp-rank
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal cp-rank $p_N$ of completely positive matrices of order $N$ satisfies $p_N=N^2/2-N/2+O(1)$. More precisely, we prove $p_N\leq\binom{N}{2}$ for every $N\geq3$ using an analytic argument based on coordinate scaling. A computer-assisted construction gives $p_N\geq\binom{N}{2}-2$ for $14\leq N\leq208$ and for every larger $N\not\equiv1\pmod4$. In the remaining residue class, it gives $p_N\geq\binom{N}{2}-3$.

papers.title: A Lower Bound for the Pyjama Problem
papers.abstract: Let $N(\varepsilon)$ be the least number of rotations of the periodic stripe $\{(x,y):\operatorname{dist}(x,\Z)\le\varepsilon\}$ that cover the plane. We prove that $\varepsilon N(\varepsilon)\to\infty$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, answering a question of Li. More precisely, for each fixed $C>0$, $n$ stripe families in distinct directions with half-width $C/n$ leave an area fraction $e^{-2C}+o(1)$ uncovered. The error is uniform in the directions and their translations.

papers.title: A Machine-Certified Degree-7,299 Counterexample to Smale's Mean Value Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct and rigorously machine-certify an explicit polynomial p in Q(i)[z] of degree d = 7,299 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) = 1 such that all 7,298 critical points satisfy min_{p'(c)=0} |p(c)/c| in [1.00002719655422710959, 1.00002719655422710960] > 1. This reduces the lowest known rigorously certified counterexample degree for Smale's Mean Value Conjecture by a factor of 4.11x compared to the October 2026 breakthrough of Adamczewski and Colbrook (degree 29,984), while increasing the margin above 1 by 54.8x. The polynomial is constructed via an analytic Fourier-smoothed Pac-Man conformal map, Fejér-Lagrange interpolation, and bit-reversal equidistribution, and verified with zero floating-point assumptions in exact arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic alongside independent 900-digit mpmath checks and pandroots v0.31.0.

papers.title: A planar graph without four- or nine-cycles that is not three-colorable
papers.abstract: We give an 82-vertex planar graph without cycles of length four or nine that is not three-colorable. Steinberg conjectured in 1976 that planar graphs without cycles of length four or five are three-colorable; Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado disproved this, and their graph contains a nine-cycle. Lu, Wang, Wang, Bu, Montassier and Raspaud asked, as recorded by Kang, Jin and Wang, for which lengths from five to nine every planar graph without cycles of that length or of length four is three-colorable. Our graph answers the length-nine case negatively. It is built from 27 complete graphs on four vertices by Ore compositions, the edge-deletion and vertex-splitting operation of Dirac, Hajós, Gallai and Ore. It is four-critical: every proper subgraph is three-colorable. Its 136 edges attain Kostochka and Yancey's lower bound, so no four-critical graph on 82 vertices has fewer edges. Lean checks planarity, the exclusion of four- and nine-cycles, and non-three-colorability; criticality and the edge minimum rest on the written proof. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization, the search code, the certificate checkers and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.

papers.title: A uniform spectral gap and winding-flux tension on the SU(2) plaquette ladder
papers.abstract: For the periodic one-plaquette-wide SU(2) Kogut–Susskind ladder at fixed lattice spacing and every even length L ≥ 2, we give a computer-assisted argument for a full spectral gap exceeding one fundamental-link electric energy throughout 0 ≤ x = λ/e ≤ 12.25, and exceeding 0.46 through x = 16. All link representations are retained. The winding-sector ground-energy difference per plaquette has an even-length thermodynamic limit. It is at least 0.5584 through x = 12, at least 0.20 through x = 30, and at least 0.1425 through x = 32. A plaquette-product trial gives an exact variational bound at arbitrary length. The spectral estimates combine a split-link reflection construction, finite-ring interval enclosures and Lean certificates. The physical realization of the formal hypotheses and the cutoff limit are paper arguments.

papers.title: An automatically generated exposition of the Casimir bound casBound_holds in Alpöge's Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: Levent Alpöge's Lean archive contains a tableau bound for the quadratic Casimir on column-alternating tensors. This automatically generated exposition explains his existing theorem casBound_holds and its coordinate proof. Its contribution is expository. The theorem bounds the real quadratic form of the slot Casimir on a union of whole columns by the squared tensor norm times an explicit coefficient in the tableau label multiplicities. Alpöge's proof bounds the swaps from one outside box into a column together, using one squared norm, and then counts the contributions by label. An AI-run survey found no explanation of the theorem in nine write-ups of the proof. On a separate theorem, typePrimesN, two independent AI graders found that the pipeline captured seven of eight insights in a hidden key before review and all eight after revision, with no incorrect keyed insights in either version.

papers.title: An Improved Lower Bound S(3, t) >= 3t - 4 for Positive Solutions of Bivariate Trinomial-t-nomial Systems and an Explicit Degree-45 Eight-Root Example
papers.abstract: Let S(3, t) denote the maximum number of isolated strictly positive real solutions in R_{>0}^2 of a real bivariate polynomial system f(x, y) = g(x, y) = 0 where f is a trinomial (3 monomials) and g is a t-nomial (t >= 3 monomials). We prove by an elementary, Sard-free constructive induction that S(3, t) >= 3t - 4 for every integer t >= 3, matching Haas's sharp value S(3, 3) = 5, strictly improving the 2007 Gomez-Niles-Rojas bound 2t - 1 for every t >= 4, and increasing the asymptotic lower-bound slope by 50%. We also exhibit a compact, symmetric degree-45 integer system of type (3, 4), x^8 + y^8 - 1 = 0 and 8x^45 + 8y^45 + 35x^3 y^3 - 25xy = 0, with 8 simple strictly positive roots, plus explicit integer records for (3, 5) (11 roots) and (3, 6) (14 roots). Both main theorems (including nondegeneracy det J != 0 for all t >= 3) are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 (Mathlib4, 2,404 lines, zero sorry, standard axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only) with green GitHub Actions CI, alongside three independent computational certifications (exact BigInt IVT, pandsysroots v0.33.0, and 200-digit mpmath).

papers.title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is in AM from a zero-free half-plane of Dedekind zeta functions, after Koiran
papers.abstract: In 1996 Koiran proved, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH), that deciding whether a system of polynomial equations with integer coefficients has a complex solution (Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, HN) is in the Arthur-Merlin class AM, hence in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy. GRH enters his proof through one estimate, a count of the primes modulo which an irreducible integer polynomial has a root. We show that this estimate, with exponent $7/8+\varepsilon$ in place of $1/2$, follows in two lines from the effective Chebotarev theorem in B. Hu's preprint on the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$, and that Koiran's proof then runs with primes of an explicit, polynomial bit length. Any zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$, $\theta<1$, common to all Dedekind zeta functions suffices, for instance $\Re s>31/32$ of Cureton and Thorner: the estimate is then Frei, Sofos and Widmer's effective Chebotarev theorem, as Baldwin and Sivek used it for one polynomial in work on 3-manifold recognition, and the step to AM is Proposition 17.2 of our paper hexagon:2611.00987. So HN is in AM granted Hu's theorem or that of Cureton and Thorner. Both are unrefereed preprints of October 2026; the second is formalized in Lean according to its authors. Through published reductions that use GRH only via Koiran's theorem, the dimension problem and the parametric Nullstellensatz are then in AM, vanishing of Schubert coefficients is in AM $\cap$ coAM in types $A$-$D$, so it is not NP-hard unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level, and homogeneous systems of parameters are constructible in $\mathrm{FP}^{\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}}$. Andrews, Garg and Schost placed HN in the counting hierarchy with no hypothesis; AM is the smaller class. Produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, written by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked it.

papers.title: Infinitely many Wilson primes on the curves y^2 = x^p - x + a
papers.abstract: For an odd prime p and a nonzero a in F_p let A = F_p[x,y]/(y^2 - x^p + x - a), the coordinate ring of a curve of genus (p-1)/2 with one point at infinity. With the notion of Wilson prime of Hexagon 2611.01011, we prove: if P in F_p[y] is irreducible and P(y) is a prime element of A, then P(y) is a Wilson prime if and only if P'' = 0. We deduce that each of these rings has infinitely many Wilson primes, given explicitly: for p >= 5 the binomials y^t - c, with c a primitive root modulo p and t running through the powers of a suitable prime divisor of p-1 that are congruent to 1 modulo p. The proof rests on the criterion of Hexagon 2611.01011 and on the fact that, on any curve y^2 = f(x) in odd characteristic, the correction term of that criterion vanishes for the prime elements that are polynomials in y. The criterion is the exact analogue of Thakur's criterion for F_q[t].

papers.title: Kostant's tori in apposition: the Borel subgroups are opposite
papers.abstract: On 22 October 1969 Grothendieck wrote to Kostant about pairs of maximal tori $T$, $T'$ of a complex simple adjoint group in apposition, $T'$ being the centraliser of a cyclic element. Choosing Borel subgroups $B \supset T$ and $B' \supset T'$, he asked whether $B$ and $B'$ are always in general position. The answer is yes, in every type and for all $|W|$ Borel subgroups through $T'$: every one of them is opposite to $B$, and also to the opposite Borel subgroup $B^-$. The proof takes a few lines from two published facts: $\operatorname{Lie}T'$ contains an element of $f + \mathfrak b$ with $f$ a principal nilpotent of $\mathfrak b^-$ (Kostant), and a Borel subalgebra containing such an element is opposite to $\mathfrak b$ (an argument of Bălibanu's). We give it in full, self-contained. In type $A$ the element of $f+\mathfrak b$ is the inverse of the cyclic element, and the statement becomes the transversality of the flags stable under a cyclic weighted shift, which we prove directly and formalise in Lean 4 with Mathlib, together with the flag forms in types $B$, $C$ and in part $D$. A computation modulo primes checks types $B_2$ to $B_7$ independently. For Grothendieck's second question, on a distinguished conjugacy class of quadruples invariant under the exterior automorphisms, the answer is no in type $A_{2l}$, where the exterior automorphism fixes no class; in the other types we computed, a construction with the Coxeter plane gives a canonical pair of invariant classes, exchanged by the sign of $e_{-\theta}$. This second part is conditional on a description of $N(T)\cap N(T')$ that no specialist has checked.

papers.title: Non-effective finite equivalence relations on finite schemes over a field: Venken's example checked, and a second one
papers.abstract: In 1961 Grothendieck asked whether a closed equivalence relation on a finite scheme over a field, with finite but not necessarily flat projections, is always effective. In a lecture at Buffalo in 1973 he still called the question open. It had been answered in the negative in 1971 by Venken, in a two-page note about the descent of flat modules whose Corollary 3.1 is a non-effective equivalence relation on the spectrum of a local Artin algebra of dimension $33$ in six variables, over any field. We give a second example, in two variables, of length $15$ ($16$ in characteristic $2$), obtained by restricting Raicu's non-effective relation on the affine plane to a finite subscheme cut out by squares of invariant functions. It is proved by hand, in every characteristic at once: a general lemma reduces the comparison of the two ideals in degree $5$ to the subalgebra $C$ generated by three invariant functions, and a linear form on the degree-$5$ part of $A \otimes_C A$ separates the obstruction. The example is shorter than Venken's; no minimality is claimed. We then recheck Venken's example by linear algebra, where the ideal of his relation exceeds, by one dimension in degree $4$, the ideal of $X \times_Y X$, $Y$ the quotient; this check is formalised in Lean, over any nonzero commutative ring, except for the dimension counts. The computer checks of both examples, over $\mathbb{Q}$ and over the finite prime fields that the pivots require, are reported separately from the proofs.

papers.title: Orbit closures of generic rational polygons with at least five sides
papers.abstract: Mirzakhani and Wright attach to the angles $\theta$ of a rational polygon the orbit closure $\mathcal M(\theta)$ of the unfolding of almost every polygon with these angles. They ask whether, for more than four sides, $\mathcal M(\theta)$ can be anything other than a connected component of a stratum of Abelian differentials or a locus of double covers of a component of a stratum of quadratic differentials. It cannot. For every choice of five or more angles, $\mathcal M(\theta)$ is the component of its stratum if the least common denominator $k$ of the angles divided by $\pi$ is odd, and the locus of holonomy double covers of the component of its quadratic stratum if $k$ is even. When some $s$ of the angles sum to $(s-1)\pi$, Apisa and Aygun treat this case by a different method; our proof does not depend on theirs. We read the rank of $\mathcal M(\theta)$ off characters of the deck rotation of the unfolding and induct on the number of sides by colliding two vertices; where no collision applies, arithmetic modulo $k$ takes its place. We also extend Mirzakhani and Wright's nonvanishing of the second fundamental form from triangles to every number of sides.

papers.title: Orbit closures of generic rational quadrilaterals
papers.abstract: Delecroix and Rüth conjectured that their lists of admissible and reduced rational triangle and quadrilateral types whose unfoldings do not have dense orbits in their ambient strata are complete, and they proved this for quadrilaterals with angles $2\pi a_i/N$ when $N\le32$. We prove the conjecture for quadrilaterals, for the generic quadrilateral with given angles. For every admissible and reduced type outside their seven quadrilateral exceptions, the orbit closure of the unfolding of the generic member is a connected component of a stratum of Abelian differentials if $N$ is odd or $N\equiv2\pmod4$, and the locus of holonomy double covers of a component of a stratum of quadratic differentials if $4$ divides $N$. The proof reads the rank of the orbit closure off a set of characters of the deck rotation of the unfolding, a cyclic cover of the sphere. Mirzakhani and Wright's rules, as extended for triangles in the two earlier papers of this series, constrain this set, and two further inputs bring in the orbit closures of triangles: the collision of two vertices, through Mirzakhani and Wright's boundary theorem, and symmetric members of the family of cyclic covers, which cover unfoldings of triangles. Parts of the proof, including a census up to $N=1000$, are computer-assisted.

papers.title: Orbit closures of scalene rational triangles: every denominator
papers.abstract: Delecroix and Rüth conjectured that, apart from an explicit list, the unfoldings of rational triangles and quadrilaterals without a reflection symmetry have dense $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbits in their ambient strata, and proved this for the triangles with angles $p_i\pi/N$ and $N\le58$. We prove the conjecture for triangles. If a scalene rational triangle is not on their list of three infinite families and nine triangles, the orbit closure of its unfolding is the connected component of its stratum when $N$ is odd, and the locus of holonomy double covers of a connected component of a stratum of quadratic differentials when $N$ is even. With the first paper of this series, it follows that the orbit is not dense in that locus for the triangles on the list, except possibly for the triangle with angles $(3\pi/20,\pi/5,13\pi/20)$. Most of the proof concerns subgroups of the units modulo $N$; parts of it, including all of $N\le58$, are computer-assisted.

papers.title: Orbit closures of scalene rational triangles: rank one and prime denominators
papers.abstract: The unfolding of a rational triangle is a translation surface, and the closure of its $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbit has a rank, which is one for lattice surfaces. We determine the scalene rational triangles of rank one: besides the known lattice triangles, which form three infinite families and four further triangles, they are the two triangles found by Delecroix and Rüth's computer search, with angles $(\pi/10,3\pi/10,3\pi/5)$ and $(\pi/12,\pi/4,2\pi/3)$, whose unfoldings are Prym eigenforms. We also prove that for a scalene triangle with angles $p_i\pi/N$, $N$ prime, the orbit closure of the unfolding is a connected component of its stratum. Delecroix and Rüth conjectured that the scalene triangles whose unfoldings do not have dense orbits in their ambient strata form an explicit list. The second theorem proves this for prime denominators, and by the first, every scalene triangle of rank one whose unfolding does not have a dense orbit in its ambient stratum is on their list. The proofs differentiate the holomorphic eigenforms of the unfolding's rotational symmetry along every direction of the orbit closure; at a prime denominator this leaves a statement about subgroups of the units modulo $N$, proved with character sums, a count of lattice points and a computation.

papers.title: Prescribed oscillating spectra and isomorphism types in $C[0,1]$
papers.abstract: The oscillating spectrum of a closed subspace of $C[0,1]$ is the set of points at which its unit ball fails to be equicontinuous. Given nonempty $F_\sigma$ sets $A,B\subseteq[0,1]$, we prove that every closed subspace with spectrum $A$ is nonisomorphic to every closed subspace with spectrum $B$ if and only if one set is countable and the other is nonmeager. We show that a countable spectrum forces the dual to be separable, while a nonmeager spectrum forces the dual to be nonseparable. For every uncountable meager $F_\sigma$ set $M$ and every separable infinite-dimensional real Banach space $E$, we construct an isomorphic copy of $E$ in $C[0,1]$ with spectrum $M$. We also show that every nonempty $F_\sigma$ set admits an uncomplemented realization. For a prescribed nonempty finite spectrum, we show that an infinite-dimensional Banach space admits a realization precisely when it embeds isomorphically into $c_0$. Using the Schreier family, we construct a norm-one complemented subspace of $C[0,1]$ with compact countably infinite spectrum that does not embed isomorphically into $c_0$. This example and the classification of pairs answer Questions~4.3 and~4.9, respectively, of Enflo, Gurariy, and Seoane-Sep\'ulveda.

papers.title: Resurgence of the squeezed Kerr oscillator: tunnel splittings, Kummer connection, and a perturbative/non-perturbative relation
papers.abstract: The squeezed (two-photon-driven) Kerr oscillator $H=a^{\dagger2}a^2-\epsilon_2(a^{\dagger2}+a^2)-\Delta a^\dagger a$, in units of the Kerr constant, underlies the Kerr-cat qubit. Its two wells at $a=\pm\alpha$, $\alpha^2=\epsilon_2+\Delta/2$, carry doublets of nearly degenerate cat states. We give the resurgent structure of these doublets at fixed detuning $\Delta$ as $\epsilon_2\to\infty$. The splitting of the $n$th doublet is \[ E_{\mathrm{odd},n}-E_{\mathrm{even},n}=\frac{8\epsilon_2(4\epsilon_2)^{2n-\Delta/2}\,\ee^{-2\epsilon_2}}{n!\,\Gamma(n-\Delta/2)}\,\big(1+O(\epsilon_2^{-1})\big). \] In the Bargmann representation, the factor $1/\Gamma(n-\Delta/2)$ is a Kummer connection coefficient, and its zeros are the known exact degeneracies at $\Delta=2m\ge 2n$. At fixed $\Delta$ and leading order, the known large-detuning WKB formula is the same expression with $\Gamma(1+\Delta/2)$ replaced by its Stirling approximation. The Rayleigh--Schr\"odinger series of each level in $1/\alpha^2$, computed exactly through order $150$, diverges as $\Gamma(j+4n-\Delta)4^{-j}$ with the prefactor fixed by the splitting, and converges at $\Delta=2$ for $n=0$. The median Borel sum of the $n=0$ series reproduces the center of the exact ground doublet up to a real two-instanton term, which a quantization condition obtained from the same matching predicts at leading order. Finally, the corrections $1+k_1/\epsilon_2+k_2/\epsilon_2^2+\cdots$ to the splitting obey a relation of Dunne--\"Unsal type with the perturbative energies: the predicted closed forms---for $k_1$ in $n$ and $\Delta$ (checked for $n\le2$ and at $(n,\Delta)=(3,2)$), $k_2$ (checked for $n\le2$), and $k_3$ (checked for $n=0$)---agree with the values extracted from exact splittings, including $k_2$ for $n=2$ and $k_3$ for $n=0$, which were not used to find the relation. With three correction terms, the formula agrees with exact diagonalization to a relative error below $2\times10^{-5}$ for $-1\le\Delta\le3$ at $\epsilon_2\ge10$ (including the limit at the exact zeros), and below $2\times10^{-4}$ for $-1\le\Delta\le11$ at $\epsilon_2=30$.

papers.title: Smooth convergents and the size of the next denominator
papers.abstract: Suppose an irrational $\xi$ has infinitely many continued-fraction convergents $P/q$ for which $|P|$, $q$, and the next denominator $Q$ have all their prime factors in a fixed finite set $S$. Marques proved that $\log Q\gg q^c$ at those indices for some $c>0$. When $S$ consists of two primes, the bound holds with $c=1$, which is sharp. When $S$ consists of three primes, the supremal exponent is at most $1/2$. In every fixed open subinterval of $(1,2)$, the minimum of $\log Q$ over $\xi$ and $P/q$ in the interval has order $\sqrt q$ at infinitely many powers $q$ of each prime in $S$. Let $N_q$ be the least $S$-smooth integer greater than $1$ congruent to $\pm1\pmod q$. For each $S$ with at least three primes, a single irrational realizes $P Q=N_q$ infinitely often.

papers.title: The constant term in Cramer's mean-square theorem for the primes. Second-order asymptotics and limiting fluctuations of the prime energy
papers.abstract: Let $I(X)=\int_1^X(\psi(x)-x)^2x^{-2}\,dx$ be the energy of the primes. Under the Riemann hypothesis (RH) and simple zeros its slope is $C_B=2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi$ (Cram\'er). We study the next terms. Under RH, simple zeros and an additional spacing condition (H$^*$), $I(X)=C_B\log X+K+\Phi(\log X)+O(X^{-1/2})$, where $\Phi$ is an absolutely convergent almost periodic sum over pairs of zeros. The constant has a closed form without zeros, $K=\frac12C_B^2-C_B-\sigma_2+2(1+\gamma_E)\log2\pi-(\log4\pi-1)^2-1+2\sum_n\Lambda(n)\varphi(1/n)$, with $\sigma_2=\sum_\rho\rho^{-2}$ and $\varphi(y)=y-\operatorname{artanh}y-\frac y2\log(1-y^2)$; under RH, $K=2.512479790006\ldots$, certified to $6\cdot10^{-13}$ in interval arithmetic. Under RH and simple zeros alone, $K$ is the Ces\`aro mean in $\log X$ of $I(X)-C_B\log X$ if and only if $\sum_{0<|\gamma-\gamma'|<\varepsilon}|\rho\rho'|^{-1}=o(\varepsilon)$: a pair of zeros at distance $\lambda$ acts like a double zero for $\log X\ll1/\lambda$. Under (H$^*$), $I(X)-C_B\log X$ has a limiting logarithmic distribution with mean $K$ and variance $V$, an explicit double sum over zeros under linear independence, whose factors we check on finite sets of zeros; numerically $V=1.2502\cdot10^{-5}$ under LI. The primes up to $10^9$ agree with the zero side to $1.3\cdot10^{-5}$ (r.m.s.) and give $K=2.512484$. In the random models of the primes and of $\mu$ that we examine the median energy is $8$ to $150$ times larger. A Gaussian-window identity isolates the principal mode of each zero in the prime signal: a closed ellipse on the line, an expanding spiral off it. A final section assembles the slope, the intercept and the oscillation as one calibrated instrument, the energy gauge, with a multiplicity-meter reading of the slope and a ledger reading of the intercept, and runs it on the primes to $10^8$ beside $38$ zeros computed from scratch.

papers.title: The divisor cross-energy has all its zeros on the critical line. Genealogy of the zeros of the reflected cross-energy and the Epstein control
papers.abstract: Cut by divisors, the reflected cross-energy of the Riemann zeta function has all its zeros on the critical line. For every $m$, with $M=m\,\mathrm{rad}(m)$, the divisor cross-energy $D_m(s)=M^{s-1}\sigma_{-s}(m)+M^{-s}\sigma_{s-1}(m)$ has all its zeros on $\re s=\frac12$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:divisor}). The Euler product factorizes the cut over the primes, and the Enestr\"om--Kakeya theorem, applied prime by prime, gives $|E_m(s)|>|E_m(1-s)|$ for $\re s>\frac12$; the ratio $\sqrt p$ between consecutive coefficients is what places the line at $\frac12$. With the coefficients of the Epstein zeta function of $x^2+5y^2$ on the same divisors (pole, functional equation, nonnegative coefficients, no Euler product) there are $12$ zeros off the line. The cut by size behaves differently. The reflected cross-energy $\CFR(N,s)=N^{-s}X_{N-1}(1-s)+N^{s-1}X_{N-1}(s)$, $X_N(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$, is a finite sum of hyperbolic cosines with positive coefficients, and for $N=2$ all its zeros lie on the critical line. As $N$ grows, zeros leave the line. For $\zeta$ they are transient: they sit at the heights of the zeros of $\zeta$ and their distance to the line decays like $1.1/\sqrt N$ ($0.144$ at $N\approx40$, $0.033$ at $N=1200$). For the Davenport--Heilbronn function the same construction keeps a permanent zero at $0.81+85.70i$, and for the Epstein function it keeps permanent zeros near $\sigma=0.9$. The passage from the divisor cut to the size cut is the convergence of partial Euler products in the strip, which is known to be equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. The translation law at the zeros, $\lambda_\rho X_n(\rho)X_n(1-\rho)=n+\frac12+\frac{\lambda_\rho}{12n}+O(n^{-2})$ with $\lambda_\rho=\rho(1-\rho)$, holds for every zero on or off the line, and the Epstein function realizes it with a complex slope: pole, functional equation, positivity and the translation law are compatible with zeros off the line. We add three tools: the exact recursion $E_{N+1}=(\frac{N+1}N)^{s-1}(E_N+\frac1N)$ of the Hermite--Biehler pair; a ladder that brackets each zero from the previous ones, $R_k^{-1/k}\le\lambda_{n+1}\le R_k/R_{k+1}$; and the correction of the harmonic-function criterion of \cite{Ca17}, whose limit is $\frac1{2\lambda}$ and not $0$, which moves its zero-finding algorithm from $25.0083$, $30.4356$ to $25.0109$, $30.4248$ (true $25.010858$, $30.424876$). We also write the logarithm of the symmetrized Euler product as a cross-energy over the primes, $\sum_p2p^{-1/2}\cosh((s-\frac12)\log p)$, and locate its singularities on a ladder of lines $\re s=\frac1{2k},1-\frac1{2k}$. Finally, the arithmetic part of $\CFR$ is $\zeta(s)$ times an explicit nonvanishing factor, so $\CFR$ decides the Riemann hypothesis only through a Tur\'an-type criterion for a finite sum $T_N$, whose zeros, unlike those of the partial sums, stay out of $\sigma>\frac12$ up to $t\approx3$--$6N$; and $\zeta(s)=\frac12s(s+1)(J(s)-\frac1{\lambda_s})$ with $J$ the Mellin transform of the positive weight $\{x\}(1-\{x\})$, so that the zeros are the points where $J=1/\lambda$.

papers.title: The Selberg integral at polynomial lengths and pair correlation beyond one
papers.abstract: For every sufficiently large $T$, Montgomery's normalized form factor is at least $0.500001$ throughout $1\le\alpha\le1.0000009$, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for $\zeta$. On a second, wider interval a smaller positive increment also improves the line $3/2-\alpha$. The arithmetic result is unconditional. For $1\le h\le X^{0.001}$, the Selberg integral on $[X,2X]$ exceeds $Xh\{\tfrac12\log(X/h^3)+a\log X\}$ with an absolute $a>0$ for all sufficiently large $X$. We obtain the increment from a second family of Ramanujan sums, supported beyond the square root. The argument also gives the form-factor increment unconditionally for complex differences of zeta zeros.

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ho,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ho(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ho$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

papers.title: Towards a conformal field theory of critical percolation. III. Quantitative mixed fusion and subleading fields
papers.abstract: How does the field produced by closing a small disk arise when two density marks approach each other in critical site percolation on the triangular lattice? We show that the contribution proportional to the scalar field E◦ accumulates over the scales at which the two marked clusters can first merge. After subtracting this logarithmic term from the rescaled, centered density pair, we construct a local field L_ℓ at reference length ℓ. The limit holds in variation norm on the full connectivity record of a surrounding circle, which allows us to derive its conformal transformation law before choosing an exterior observation. We then bring E^◦ or L_r to distance r from a further density mark. After angular averaging and subtraction of the leading density, we obtain expansions with error O(r^(61/40)) at fixed observation radius. The scalar null identity cancels the possible r^(55/48) term for E^◦, leaving r^(3/2)Ψ. For L_r we identify the coefficient of r^(3/2)Ψ and isolate a possible contribution of order r^(55/48). The passage to arbitrary exterior observations uses joint convergence of the connections among interior marks and labelled boundary arcs in the domains left by an exploration.

papers.title: Unimodality of the number of parking functions with a given maximum displacement
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every n, the numbers of parking functions of length n in which the maximum displacement of a car from its preferred spot is 0, 1, . . . , n−1 form a unimodal sequence. This confirms a conjecture of Celano, Elder, Hadaway, Harris, Martin, Priestley and Udell. The proof follows, for each value of the maximum displacement, the sign of the difference of two neighbouring terms as n grows. It is computer-assisted: explicit estimates are used when the displacement is large, and exact computations with integers, carried out by computer, when the displacement or the length is small.

papers.title: Wilson primes for an elliptic coordinate ring of class number one
papers.abstract: Thakur characterised the Wilson primes of F_q[t] (q odd) as the primes with vanishing second derivative, and asked for generalisations to other function fields, for instance of class number one. Let A = F_3[x,y]/(y^2 - x^3 + x + 1), the coordinate ring of an elliptic curve with a single rational point; it is a principal ideal domain. We define a Wilson product W_d in A which reduces to Thakur's F_d in genus 0 and satisfies W_d = -1 mod pi for every prime pi of degree d. We prove that pi is a Wilson prime, i.e. W_d = -1 mod pi^2, if and only if D^2 pi = 0 and the coefficient of the monomial of degree d-1 in pi vanishes, where D is the invariant derivation. The second condition has no counterpart in genus 0. There is no Wilson prime of degree d = 1 mod 3, and y^(4*25^k) + y^(25^k) - 1 (k >= 0) is an infinite family of Wilson primes. The criterion is confirmed by exact computation on all 25430 primes of degree at most 11.

papers.title: Wilson primes for coordinate rings of hyperelliptic curves with one point at infinity
papers.abstract: Let A = F_q[x,y]/(y^2+h(x)y-f(x)) be the coordinate ring of a smooth affine curve of genus g >= 1 with one point at infinity (deg f = 2g+1, deg h <= g), in any characteristic; A need not be principal. With the Wilson product W_d of Hexagon 2611.01007 and 2611.01009, a prime element pi of degree d is called a Wilson prime if W_d = -1 mod pi^2. We prove that W_d = -1 + pi (E(pi) + K_pi D(pi)) / D(pi)^2 mod pi^2, so that pi is a Wilson prime if and only if pi divides E(pi) + K_pi D(pi), where D is the invariant derivation, E = (h^2+4f) d_x^(2) + (f' + h'(y+h)) d_x is a second order operator written with Hasse derivatives, the same in every characteristic, and K_pi is defined by a canonical decomposition; for d >= 2g it is a polynomial in x of degree less than g, given by an explicit recipe in terms of the leading coefficients of pi. This contains the divisibility criteria of the two earlier notes for the four rings of class number one, and Thakur's criterion for F_q[t] has the same shape. The statement is confirmed by exact computation on 17 curves of genus 1, 2, 3 in characteristics 2, 3, 5, 7.

papers.title: Wilson primes for the coordinate rings of class number one in characteristic two
papers.abstract: Besides the polynomial rings, four coordinate rings A of a curve over a finite field minus one rational point have class number one. For the one of characteristic 3, the Wilson primes were characterised in Hexagon 2611.01007. We treat the three rings of characteristic 2: y^2+y=x^3+x+1 over F_2, y^2+y=x^3+alpha over F_4, and y^2+y=x^5+x^3+1 over F_2 (genus 2). A prime pi of degree d is a Wilson prime, i.e. W_d = -1 mod pi^2, if and only if pi divides D2(pi) + (f' + kappa) D(pi), where D = d/dx, D2 is the second Hasse derivative and kappa is an explicit function of the leading coefficients of pi. In genus 1 this is equivalent to D2(pi) = t D(t pi) with t = x + a, a explicit, and there is no Wilson prime of degree 0 or 3 mod 4. In genus 2 it is equivalent to D2(pi) + (x^4+x^2+kappa) D(pi) = (x^2+x+1+kappa) pi for d >= 4, and there is no Wilson prime of degree 2 or 3 mod 4, d >= 4. The criteria are confirmed by exact computation on 15302 primes. The product W_d refers to the given model of the ring.
